proofs.text: Call `record_label()` on a record that is not committed; verify `local`. Commit it as a person; verify `developer`. Commit it with the committer `GitHub <noreply@github.com>`, the author `github-actions[bot]` and a good signature; verify `ci`. Commit the same identities unsigned with no gpg on the machine; verify `ci`. Commit them unsigned with gpg present; verify `developer`. Commit them signed with a key this checkout has no allowed-signers file for, so `%G?` reads `N`, with gpg present; verify `ci`. Commit it as the Azure DevOps build service with no signature; verify `ci`

reasons: PROOF-9 happy_path_only: No proof of this rule names a rejection, an error or a boundary.
rule_text: A record is labelled from the last commit that touched it: `ci` when the git host made it, which on GitHub is the committer email `noreply@github.com` with the author `github-actions[bot]` and on Azure DevOps the build service, and only when the signature does not contradict that identity; `developer` when a person did; `local` when it is not committed at all
